subject: SummitEdge: latency & throughput qualification + ops cadence
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Mike Alvarez <mike.alvarez@summitedge.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 9 May 2029 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + next steps from today’s latency/throughput deep dive

Hi Mike / Priya —

Thanks for taking the time today. Short recap from our side so we have a single source of truth and clear next steps. I’ve attached a draft SLO matrix and a quick topology sketch that we discussed.

Key pain points you shared
- End users expect median response < 200ms for short intents (<=64 tokens) and p95 < 450ms for combined multi-turn workflows.
- Cost is a constraint for high-volume reranking (10–15M calls/mo) — need unit-cost targets to justify Dedicated vs Hosted.
- On-prem data residency for PII-enriched prompts in EU/US subsets; currently evaluating VPC/private deployment.

Goals we aligned on
- Proof-of-concept: meet p95 latency <= 450ms for the 64–256 token window with 95% availability during business hours (US-PST).
- Throughput baseline: sustain 1,200 concurrent QPS for short prompts with graceful degradation to lower-cost model variants under burst.
- Cost target: unit token cost reduction of >= 35% vs your current baseline after batching/quantization.

Technical takeaways
- Model: you’ll start with a 13B decoder model (custom tuned). We recommend a 16k kv-cache aware variant for the multi-turn paths.
- Topology: a primary Dedicated pool in us-west for latency-critical traffic + a fallback Hosted variant in us-east with auto-routing. See attached sketch.
- Caching/batching: prefix caching for common intents + dynamic batching up to 32 tokens for QPS spikes.
- Fallback policy: route non-critical low-SLA requests to a quantized 8-bit model variant.

Action items (owners & ETA)
1) Olga: share SLO matrix + topology sketch (attached) and a rough cost model by EOD tomorrow — 2029-05-10 EOD PT.
2) Mike/Priya: confirm data residency constraints and whether you need on-prem package for all PII traffic — by 2029-05-13.
3) Markus: provide Dedicated pool sizing option and burst policy draft — by 2029-05-12.
4) Karthik: checklist for procurement (security artifacts + SOC2 evidence) and timeline — by 2029-05-12.

Attachments: rdw_slo_matrix.xlsx (draft), summitedge_topology_sketch.png (sketch)

Thanks again — I’ll loop in Solutions Engineering if we get confirmation on the on-prem scope.

— Olga
Olga Petrov
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Redwood Inference

From: Mike Alvarez <mike.alvarez@summitedge.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Ranganathan <priya.r@summitedge.com>
Date: Thu, 9 May 2029 14:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps from today’s latency/throughput deep dive

Thanks Olga — this is really helpful and aligned with what we heard internally. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Residency: we need on-prem or VPC-only handling for any prompts that contain electoral roll data or customer PII. That affects ~22% of traffic during peak hours; the rest can be routed to a cloud-hosted pool.
2) Availability window: 8am–6pm PT is our critical SLO window, weekends best-effort.
3) Model variants: confirmed — we want to evaluate a 13B tuned model + fallback 7B quantized for low-cost tasks.

We’ll confirm the procurement constraints by Monday (2029-05-13). For the POC timeline: we’re aiming for an internal pilot in late June.

Quick ask: can you include a conservative cost projection (per-1k tokens) for Hosted vs Dedicated in your EOD note so we can budget?

— Mike
Mike Alvarez
Head of ML Infrastructure | SummitEdge
mike.alvarez@summitedge.com

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 9 May 2029 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps from today’s latency/throughput deep dive

Looping in a few quick procurement/security items we’ll need to unblock Dedicated sizing and timeline: 
- Confirm TLS mutual auth + customer-managed KMS for any VPC/on-prem package.
- If SummitEdge requires on-prem, we need their infra point-of-contact and a brief network diagram.
- SOC2 artifacts: we can provide our SOC2 Type II report and a limited evidence bundle; procurement will want specific retention and logging SLAs.

I’ll draft a Dedicated pool sizing short-list based on their concurrency target and promised p95 — will share by Sunday (2029-05-12).

-Markus
Director, Solutions Architecture
Redwood Inference
